chung.Description:
Main objective: This course equips students with comprehensive foundation and specialized knowledge of hotel housekeeping operations. Learners will develop skills in managing resources, controlling costs and human resources, delivering quality service, problem-solving and responding to operational incidents, applying professional standards and fostering environmental awareness, to meet the demands of modern hospitality management.

-Description: Housekeeping Operations explores core and advanced functions of the hotel housekeeping department, including cleaning and inspection procedures for guest rooms and public areas, inventory and equipment management, cost control, human resource management, laundry and maintenance supervision, service quality enhancement, guest complaint handling, and special event support. The course emphasizes teamwork, discipline, professional attitude, and effective communication for multicultural settings.

-Teaching method: The course applies diverse pedagogical approaches such as lectures, analytical discussions, skills demonstrations, collaborative group work, roleplay, case studies, problem-based learning, and project planning for service scenarios. Assessment is integrated through applied exercises, situational analysis, and teamwork performance.

- Facility and equipment requirement : Depending on the training condition of each campus, the course will be implemented in school lab designed up to 4-5* hotel standard, real hotel or other places, which fully met with requirements.

-Completion Criteria:

Every on-going assessment component > 0; Final Result >=5 & Final Exam Score >= 4

clo: Analyze the role, organizational structure, and functions of the housekeeping department within hotels, and identify modern operational trends in the hospitality industry.
Apply standardized procedures for inspecting and servicing guest rooms, public areas, and specialized equipment to ensure service quality and safety.
Assess and monitor specifications for supplies, chemicals, and equipment used in housekeeping, in compliance with safety regulations and cost-control practices.
Operate and supervise maintenance tasks, laundry services, inventory distribution, guest guidance, ensuring hotel standards and occupational safety.
Manage human resources in the housekeeping department: planning staff allocation, training programs, performance evaluation, and promoting teamwork and discipline.
Analyze principles of cost control, manage consumables inventory, establish stock auditing procedures, and prepare periodic housekeeping cost reports.
Propose methods to enhance service quality, develop processes for handling guest complaints, and practice effective and professional communication in a multicultural hotel environment.
Plan, organize, and coordinate the provision of additional services (flowers, beverages, gifts, decorations) to meet special guest requirements for events and small functions in the hotel.
Demonstrate problem-solving skills for operational incidents (safety, emergencies, property loss, operational risks) encountered in housekeeping operations.
Commit to professional standards, uphold a positive and responsible attitude, and demonstrate environmental and occupational safety awareness in all professional activities.

Each group of 4–5 students will role-play as the Housekeeping department and be assigned the task of decorating a hotel room (room type chosen by the group or designated by the lecturer) according to a specific concept for a special occasion (for example: honeymoon, birthday, small family honeymoon, MICE guests, VIP business guests, Christmas, Tết/Lunar New Year, etc.).
The group must ensure that the decoration is beautiful, safe, suitable for the target guest, within budget, and complies with the hotel’s operational standards and policies.
Minimum length of the group assignment should be 10 pages, excluding appendices

"Group presentation, and practice in class room
"

"- Concept description document (2–3 pages): target guest profile, purpose of the decoration, main theme/idea, color tone, experience message conveyed to the guest, and connection to current modern trends in the hospitality industry (CLO1, CLO7, CLO8).
- Room decoration procedure checklist: preparation steps, safety and hygiene checks, sequence of arranging each decorative item/category, and final inspection (CLO2, CLO3, CLO4, CLO6).
- Cost estimation table for decorative items (flowers, candles, balloons, gifts, special amenities, etc.), clearly stating suppliers/sources, quantity, and methods for inventory control (CLO3, CLO6).
- Staffing assignment chart and implementation timeline (who does what, duration for each task, shift arrangement if any) including occupational safety notes (CLO4, CLO5, CLO10).
- Actual photographs or mock-up/rehearsal of the room decoration done in class or in a sample room, accompanied by an internal group evaluation report detailing issues that arose and how they were resolved (CLO7, CLO9).
